input.question: If I brush my teeth twice everyday, why are they never fully white? Is there a way to get them there?
input.ground_truth: Natural, healthy teeth are not white, they are ivory colored. The desire for white teeth is an artificial standard pushed by the beauty industry, hence all the products that will whiten your teeth... for a fee.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If I brush my teeth twice everyday, why are they never fully white? Is there a way to get them there?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine your teeth are like a piece of paper. When you eat or drink things like chocolate, tea, or soda, it’s like drawing with a marker on the paper. Brushing your teeth is like wiping the paper with a cloth, but sometimes the marker doesn’t come all the way off.

Brushing your teeth every day is really good! It helps keep them healthy and stops them from getting holes (cavities). But the things that make your teeth not so white (like coffee, juice, or candy) can stick to your teeth and make them look yellow or brown over time.

Even if you brush really well, it’s hard to get all the tiny bits off every single time. That’s why your teeth might not be super, super white—even if you brush twice a day.

If you want your teeth to be extra white, you can:
- Keep brushing and flossing every day.
- Use a special toothpaste that helps make teeth brighter.
- Sometimes, grown-ups go to the dentist and get their teeth cleaned extra well, or they use special treatments at the dentist to make them whiter.

But the most important thing is to keep brushing and taking care of your teeth so they stay healthy and strong!
